name: Paracetamol
mechanism: Primarily reduces central prostaglandin synthesis and produces analgesic and antipyretic effects; its exact mechanism is not completely established.

adult.dose: 650–1,000 mg every 4–6 hours as needed
adult.maximum: Do not exceed 4,000 mg in 24 hours from all acetaminophen-containing products

pediatric.maximum: Maximum 5 doses in 24 hours; use product-specific pediatric maximums

duration: Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest appropriate duration.
dosage.renalAdjustment: Dose interval may need extension in severe renal impairment; follow product-specific guidance.
dosage.hepaticAdjustment: Use caution in hepatic impairment, chronic alcohol use, malnutrition, or dehydration.
dosage.reference: Acetaminophen/Paracetamol official prescribing information; verify formulation-specific labeling before clinical use.

contraindications: Severe hypersensitivity to acetaminophen/paracetamol
Severe active liver disease is a major caution
adverseEffects: Hepatotoxicity with overdose or excessive cumulative exposure
interactions: Warfarin with prolonged regular use may increase anticoagulant effect
Other acetaminophen-containing products increase overdose risk
monitoring: Total daily dose from all sources

name: Ibuprofen
mechanism: Reversibly inhibits cyclooxygenase enzymes, reducing prostaglandin synthesis and producing analgesic, antipyretic, and anti-inflammatory effects.

adult.dose: 200–400 mg every 4–6 hours as needed for OTC use
adult.maximum: 1,200 mg/day for OTC self-care; prescription dosing may differ

adult.dose: Individualized prescription dosing, commonly 400–800 mg three or four times daily

pediatric.indication: Pain or fever in children 6 months and older

duration: Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration.
dosage.renalAdjustment: Avoid or use great caution in significant renal impairment; NSAIDs can worsen renal function.

contraindications: Known serious hypersensitivity to ibuprofen/NSAIDs
History of aspirin/NSAID-induced asthma, urticaria, or allergic-type reactions
Perioperative use in CABG surgery
interactions: Anticoagulants/antiplatelets may increase bleeding risk
ACE inhibitors/ARBs and diuretics may increase renal risk
Lithium levels may increase

name: Amoxicillin
mechanism: Binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis, causing bacterial cell death in susceptible organisms.

adult.indication: Mild to moderate ENT, skin, or genitourinary infection
adult.dose: 250 mg every 8 hours or 500 mg every 12 hours

adult.indication: Severe ENT, skin, genitourinary, or lower respiratory infection
adult.dose: 500 mg every 8 hours or 875 mg every 12 hours

pediatric.indication: Mild to moderate infection in children >3 months and <40 kg
pediatric.dose: 20 mg/kg/day divided every 8 hours or 25 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours

pediatric.indication: Severe infection in children >3 months and <40 kg
pediatric.dose: 40 mg/kg/day divided every 8 hours or 45 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours
Up to 30 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours

duration: Duration depends on infection and clinical response.
Streptococcus pyogenes infections generally require at least 10 days.
dosage.renalAdjustment: Dose reduction or interval adjustment is required in significant renal impairment.
dosage.hepaticAdjustment: No routine hepatic dose adjustment is generally required, but monitor clinically in significant hepatic disease.

contraindications: Serious hypersensitivity to amoxicillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics
interactions: Warfarin may have altered anticoagulant effect
Allopurinol may increase rash risk
Methotrexate toxicity may increase
monitoring: Renal function when prolonged therapy or renal impairment is present

name: Azithromycin
mechanism: Binds the 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis.
uses: Acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis
Selected sexually transmitted and other susceptible infections

adult.dose: 500 mg once daily on day 1, then 250 mg once daily on days 2–5
adult.maximum: 500 mg on day 1, then 250 mg/day in this regimen

adult.indication: Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis
adult.dose: 500 mg once daily for 3 days, or 500 mg on day 1 followed by 250 mg daily on days 2–5

adult.indication: Selected uncomplicated genital infection due to Chlamydia trachomatis
adult.dose: 1 g orally as a single dose in labeling where applicable

pediatric.dose: 10 mg/kg on day 1, then 5 mg/kg/day on days 2–5, or other labeled regimens depending on age/indication
10 mg/kg on day 1, then 5 mg/kg/day on days 2–5

duration: Common oral regimens are 3–5 days depending on indication.
dosage.renalAdjustment: No routine adjustment is generally required for mild to moderate renal impairment; severe impairment warrants caution.
dosage.hepaticAdjustment: Use caution in hepatic disease because azithromycin is substantially hepatically handled.

contraindications: History of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction associated with prior azithromycin use
Serious hypersensitivity to macrolides
interactions: Other QT-prolonging drugs may increase arrhythmia risk
Warfarin effect may change
Digoxin levels may increase in some patients

name: Ceftriaxone
mechanism: Inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding proteins.
uses: Gonococcal infection in appropriate current guideline-based regimens

adult.dose: 1–2 g once daily, or divided into two doses
Use current local/CDC guideline-based ceftriaxone dose; historical labels may differ
1 g intravenously as a single dose 1/2–2 hours before surgery

pediatric.dose: 50–75 mg/kg/day once daily or divided twice daily
50 mg/kg intramuscularly as a single dose
Initial 100 mg/kg, followed by 100 mg/kg/day once daily or divided every 12 hours

duration: Usual duration: 4–14 days depending on infection and clinical response.
For Streptococcus pyogenes infections, treatment should continue for at least 10 days.
dosage.renalAdjustment: No dosage adjustment is generally necessary for renal impairment when used according to labeling; severe combined renal and hepatic impairment requires particular caution.
dosage.hepaticAdjustment: No dosage adjustment is generally necessary for hepatic impairment when used according to labeling; severe combined renal and hepatic impairment requires particular caution.

contraindications: Known serious hypersensitivity to ceftriaxone or relevant cephalosporins
Contraindicated in certain neonates with hyperbilirubinemia
Contraindicated in neonates requiring or expected to require calcium-containing IV solutions
interactions: Important compatibility precautions with calcium-containing IV solutions in neonates
Warfarin effect may change in susceptible patients
monitoring: Renal and hepatic status when clinically appropriate
Consider coagulation status in patients at risk of vitamin K deficiency

name: Metformin
mechanism: Reduces hepatic glucose production, decreases intestinal glucose absorption to a lesser extent, and improves insulin sensitivity and peripheral glucose utilization.
uses: Improving glycemic control with diet and exercise

adult.dose: 500 mg twice daily or 850 mg once daily with meals; titrate according to response and formulation
adult.maximum: 2,550 mg/day for immediate-release tablets in the cited labeling

pediatric.indication: Type 2 diabetes mellitus in children ≥10 years
pediatric.dose: 500 mg twice daily with meals; increase by 500 mg weekly as tolerated

duration: Long-term therapy when clinically indicated; reassess glycemic control and tolerability regularly.
dosage.renalAdjustment: Assess eGFR before initiation. Do not use if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²; initiation is not recommended at eGFR 30–45 mL/min/1.73 m².
dosage.hepaticAdjustment: Generally avoid in significant hepatic impairment because of lactic acidosis risk.

contraindications: eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m²
Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis including diabetic ketoacidosis
Serious hypersensitivity to metformin
adverseEffects: Vitamin B12 deficiency with long-term use
interactions: Cationic drugs eliminated by renal tubular secretion can increase metformin exposure
Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors may increase metabolic acidosis risk
Iodinated contrast procedures may require temporary interruption depending on renal function and clinical circumstances
monitoring: Vitamin B12 during long-term therapy when clinically appropriate

name: Insulin
mechanism: Activates insulin receptors, increasing glucose uptake and utilization while suppressing hepatic glucose production and promoting anabolic storage of carbohydrate, fat, and protein.
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus when insulin is required
Hyperglycemic emergencies using appropriate insulin protocols
Perioperative or inpatient glycemic management when indicated
routes: Intravenous for selected formulations and clinical situations

adult.dose: Individualize according to insulin formulation, meals, glucose monitoring, insulin sensitivity, and clinical situation
adult.maximum: No single fixed maximum; dosing is individualized

adult.indication: Insulin infusion for selected acute-care situations
adult.dose: Use an institution-specific protocol and the exact insulin formulation's prescribing information

pediatric.dose: Individualize total daily insulin requirement and divide among basal and prandial components

pediatric.indication: Type 2 diabetes mellitus when insulin is required
pediatric.dose: Individualize according to glucose response and treatment regimen

duration: Insulin therapy is individualized and may be lifelong depending on the condition.
Different insulin formulations have different onset, peak, and duration.
dosage.renalAdjustment: Insulin requirements may decrease with renal impairment; monitor glucose closely and individualize dosing.
dosage.hepaticAdjustment: Insulin requirements may change with hepatic impairment; monitor glucose closely and individualize dosing.
dosage.reference: DailyMed prescribing information for the specific insulin formulation

contraindications: Hypoglycemia
Hypersensitivity to the specific insulin formulation or excipients
interactions: Beta-blockers may mask some symptoms of hypoglycemia
Corticosteroids may increase glucose requirements
Other glucose-lowering drugs may increase hypoglycemia risk
source: DailyMed insulin labeling; formulation-specific information is required

name: Furosemide
mechanism: Inhibits the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, producing potent natriuresis and diuresis.
uses: Edema associated with heart failure, hepatic disease, or renal disease

adult.dose: 20–80 mg orally as an initial single dose; may be repeated or titrated according to response
adult.maximum: Up to 600 mg/day may be used in clinically severe edematous states under careful supervision

adult.dose: 80 mg/day initially, usually divided as 40 mg twice daily, then adjust to response

pediatric.dose: 2 mg/kg orally as an initial single dose; if response is inadequate, increase by 1–2 mg/kg no sooner than 6–8 hours later
pediatric.maximum: Doses >6 mg/kg are not recommended for routine oral pediatric dosing

duration: Individualize according to response and underlying disease.
dosage.renalAdjustment: Dose response may be reduced in renal impairment; careful titration and monitoring of fluid/electrolytes are required.
dosage.hepaticAdjustment: Use cautiously in severe hepatic disease because rapid electrolyte/fluid changes can precipitate complications.

contraindications: Anuria
Hypersensitivity to furosemide
adverseEffects: Ototoxicity with high or rapid parenteral dosing
interactions: NSAIDs may reduce diuretic effect and increase renal risk
Digoxin toxicity risk can increase with hypokalemia
Aminoglycosides may increase ototoxicity risk

name: Omeprazole
mechanism: Irreversibly inhibits the gastric H+/K+-ATPase proton pump in gastric parietal cells, suppressing gastric acid secretion.
uses: Duodenal and gastric ulcer disease in appropriate regimens
H. pylori eradication regimens with antibiotics

adult.dose: 20 mg once daily

adult.indication: Erosive esophagitis due to acid-mediated GERD
adult.dose: 20 mg once daily for 4–8 weeks
Starting dose 60 mg once daily; adjust to patient needs
adult.maximum: Doses above 80 mg/day should be divided; much higher doses have been used under specialist supervision

pediatric.dose: 5–20 mg once daily according to body weight
5–20 mg once daily according to body weight

duration: GERD treatment is generally limited to the shortest appropriate course; erosive esophagitis commonly requires 4–8 weeks.
dosage.renalAdjustment: No routine renal dose adjustment is generally required.
dosage.hepaticAdjustment: Dose reduction may be appropriate in hepatic impairment for some indications; follow product-specific labeling.
dosage.reference: DailyMed omeprazole delayed-release capsule prescribing information

contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to omeprazole or substituted benzimidazoles
adverseEffects: Long-term risks may include hypomagnesemia, vitamin B12 deficiency, and certain infections
interactions: Clopidogrel interaction can reduce antiplatelet activation
Warfarin effect may change
Drugs requiring acidic gastric pH for absorption may be affected
monitoring: Magnesium/B12 when long-term therapy or risk factors are present

name: Salbutamol
mechanism: Stimulates beta2-adrenergic receptors in bronchial smooth muscle, producing bronchodilation.
uses: Acute relief or prevention of bronchospasm in reversible obstructive airway disease

adult.dose: 2 inhalations every 4–6 hours; in some patients 1 inhalation every 4 hours may be sufficient
adult.maximum: More frequent administration or more inhalations than recommended are not advised without medical direction

adult.dose: 2 inhalations 15–30 minutes before exercise

pediatric.dose: 2 inhalations every 4–6 hours; in some patients 1 inhalation every 4 hours may be sufficient
pediatric.maximum: More frequent administration or more inhalations than recommended are not advised

duration: Use according to asthma/airway-disease treatment plan; frequent need for rescue medication requires clinical reassessment.
dosage.renalAdjustment: No routine adjustment for inhaled albuterol/salbutamol is generally specified.
dosage.hepaticAdjustment: No routine adjustment is generally specified for inhaled salbutamol.
dosage.reference: DailyMed albuterol sulfate inhalation aerosol prescribing information

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to albuterol/salbutamol or formulation components
interactions: Nonselective beta-blockers may antagonize bronchodilation
Other sympathomimetics may increase cardiovascular effects
Diuretics may worsen hypokalemia
monitoring: Potassium when high-dose therapy is used
source: DailyMed albuterol sulfate inhalation aerosol labeling
